rev_growth.why: Year 1 (FY2026) follows management's reported guidance of a 1.5-2.0% decline, because divestitures of about 4.5% outweigh organic growth. terminal_growth.why: Long-run growth is set slightly below the nominal anchor, because outsourced non-clinical research should grow with R&D spending but faces alternative-methods and outsourcing risks.

risks.risk: Biotech funding and pharma R&D demand weaken again, or the Create the Future savings are not delivered, so margins stall below the historical range.

situation.margin_position: The FY2025 GAAP operating margin of 0.63% is far below the company's own history of about 13-17%. It was depressed by a $165.0 million Biologics goodwill impairment, heavy amortization and accelerated depreciation, restructuring charges and a demand downturn. In 2026 the margin rebounds to about 14.8% over nine months, helped by one-offs: a $44.6 million DSA tax-reserve reversal, a $38.5 million sale-leaseback gain, and lower amortization. Underlying non-GAAP margin is about 23%, so the GAAP margin should keep recovering toward the historical range rather than staying near zero.

tax_rate_representative.why: The 17.8% base-year rate is below the statutory level, and 2026 shows large tax benefits from reserve reversals, so the sustainable rate is uncertain.

situation.why: FY2025 operating income was close to zero because of the impairment, restructuring and accelerated amortization, so it is not a usable earnings base. Demand has since improved (organic growth +4.7% in Q3, backlog up), and divestitures of the CDMO, Cell Solutions and European Discovery businesses change the revenue base. I therefore model a margin recovery from the base year and fade it to a mid-to-high teens level.

quotes: Restructuring charges were $19.2 million and $73.8 million during the three and nine months ended September 26, 2026, respectively, compared with $99.8 million and $107.0 million in fiscal 2025 and 2024, respectively.

growth_thesis.claim: Organic revenue growth, led by the Manufacturing and DSA segments, is the main underlying driver: organic revenue rose 4.7% in Q3 2026 while reported revenue fell 2.2% because of the May 2026 divestitures.
quotes: On an organic basis, revenue increased 4.7%, driven by revenue growth in the Manufacturing Solutions (Manufacturing) and Discovery and Safety Assessment (DSA) segments.
Revenue was $982.7 million, a decrease of 2.2% from $1,004.9 million in the third quarter of 2025, primarily driven by the impact of the May 2026 divestitures.

growth_thesis.basis: stated in P4; counter figures stated in P5
growth_thesis.claim: DSA demand recovery is a driver: DSA backlog rose to $2.0 billion at September 26, 2026 from $1.9 billion at December 27, 2025.
quotes: Consistent with the improving demand environment, DSA backlog increased slightly to $2.0 billion as of September 26, 2026 from $1.9 billion as of December 27, 2025.

growth_thesis.basis: condition inferred from management's stated causes in P4
growth_thesis.claim: For DSA demand to continue, biotech funding and big-pharma reinvestment in early-stage R&D pipelines must hold up, since management attributes the improvement to these factors.
quotes: We are continuing to see an improved spending environment from our client base, principally within our DSA segment, as the demand conditions have improved from levels experienced in the recent quarters, due primarily to increased biotech funding and global biopharmaceutical companies refocusing their investments on their early-stage research and development pipelines.

growth_thesis.claim: DSA net bookings and proposals rising year over year is a leading indicator cited by the CEO.
quotes: Revenue and earnings per share outperformed our prior expectations, DSA net bookings and proposals continued to show robust, year-over-year increases, and we continued to make meaningful progress towards our strategy and long-term financial targets.

growth_thesis.basis: stated in P2 as a risk factor

quotes: The outsourcing trend in non-clinical and clinical stages of drug discovery and development may decrease, which could impair our growth.

growth_thesis.basis: stated in P5; counter stated in P3

quotes: Organic revenue increased 7.4%, driven by strong demand in both the Biologics Testing Solutions and Microbial Solutions businesses.

growth_thesis.basis: stated in P5; counter stated in P4

quotes: The GAAP and non-GAAP increases were driven primarily by the benefit of the CDMO divestiture.

growth_thesis.basis: stated in P4 as management expectations
growth_thesis.claim: Cost savings programmes support earnings: the company expects about $300 million of cumulative annualized savings by the end of 2026, and Create the Future targets more than $300 million of incremental savings in 2027–2030.
quotes: Through the ongoing actions, the Company expects to achieve approximately $300 million of cumulative annualized cost savings by the end of 2026, with more than $175 million realized through fiscal 2025.
In addition, the Create the Future program is expected to generate incremental cost savings in excess of $300 million between 2027 and 2030.

growth_thesis.basis: stated in P2 as a risk factor

quotes: If we are not successful in realizing cost savings from our restructuring initiatives, our business may be adversely impacted.

growth_thesis.basis: facts stated in P4 and P5; the causal link is inferred

quotes: The preliminary purchase price for the Cambodian NHP Supplier was $507.3 million, consisting of $335.0 million paid at closing and $172.3 million representing the acquisition date fair value of deferred consideration, which is payable upon the satisfaction of certain post-close conditions.

The non-GAAP operating margin increase was primarily driven by operating leverage from higher study volume for regulated safety assessment services, as well as lower sourcing costs for large research models.

material_events.claim: The company completed the acquisition of certain assets of a Cambodian non-human primate supplier for a preliminary purchase price of $507.3 million, of which $335.0 million was paid at closing and $172.3 million was deferred consideration.

The preliminary purchase price for the Cambodian NHP Supplier was $507.3 million, consisting of $335.0 million paid at closing and $172.3 million representing the acquisition date fair value of deferred consideration, which is payable upon the satisfaction of certain post-close conditions.

material_events.claim: The company completed the acquisition of an additional 79% equity interest in PathoQuest SAS for $67.4 million.
quotes: On April 17, 2026, we completed the acquisition of an additional 79% equity interest in PathoQuest SAS (PathoQuest), for $67.4 million.

material_events.claim: The company sold certain assets at its Wilmington, Massachusetts site under a sale-leaseback and recognized a pre-tax gain of approximately $38.5 million.
quotes: In March 2026, we completed the sale of certain assets located at our Wilmington, Massachusetts site.
Upon meeting the criteria for sale leaseback, we derecognized the book value of $21.6 million and recognized a pre-tax gain of approximately $38.5 million.

material_events.claim: The company sold its CDMO and Cell Solutions businesses to GI Partners, paying the buyer net cash of $12.4 million, and recognized a pre-tax loss on divestiture of $181.7 million for the nine months, including a $118.0 million held-for-sale loss in the first quarter.
quotes: On May 6, 2026, we sold our CDMO and Cell Solutions businesses (CDMO and Cell Solutions Divestiture) to GI Partners (GI) for net cash paid to the buyer of $12.4 million, net of costs to sell and subject to certain customary closing adjustments.

These businesses and the related assets and liabilities met the criteria for held-for-sale as of March 28, 2026, resulting in a pre-tax loss of $118.0 million recognized for the three months ended March 28, 2026, which represents the excess of its carrying value over the fair value less cost to sell.
We recognized the pre-tax loss on divestiture of $181.7 million for the nine months ended September 26, 2026 within Other expense, net on the unaudited condensed consolidated statements of income.

material_events.claim: The company sold certain European Discovery Services businesses to IQVIA for $126.4 million in cash.
quotes: On May 22, 2026, we sold certain European Discovery Services businesses (European Discovery Divestiture) to IQVIA Inc. (IQVIA) for a purchase price of $126.4 million in cash, net of costs to sell and subject to certain customary closing adjustments.

(NYSE: CRL) announced today that it has entered into definitive agreements to acquire Frontage Holdings Corporation’s bioanalysis and DMPK operations in Exton, Pennsylvania for approximately $470 million in cash, subject to customary closing adjustments.
The transaction is expected to close during the first half of 2027, subject to required shareholder and regulatory approvals, and other customary closing conditions.
